A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRPO-MA research despite the changed title and framing. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original math, code, vision, and simulated-manipulation experiments, together with ablations, covariance diagnostics, and training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, trained-model configurations, benchmark evaluations, and optimization diagnostics.

M1.justification: Sampling, XML branching boundaries, reward averaging, and separate thought/answer advantages are retained. The written loss changes: v1 averages KL-containing Jclip terms separately for thoughts and answers (Eqs. 1 and 3), whereas v3 subtracts one shared KL penalty (Eq. 2). A corresponding implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Appendix G.6 adds GSM8K and HumanEval evaluations within the existing math and code domains. The original AIME2024, LiveBench, vision datasets, and simulated-manipulation coverage remain; the additions expand benchmark populations without introducing a new application domain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6 adds evaluated trajectory-prediction comparisons with GRPO-CARE, DAPO, Dr.GRPO, and TreeRPO, including TreeRPO-64 and TreeRPO-128. These substantially broaden comparison beyond v1's GRPO sampling configurations, pretrained models, and supervised baselines. The original comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 add training comparisons on Qwen2.5-VL-7B using T8A1/T8A4 and Qwen3-4B using T4A1/T4A4. New evaluations include Pass@1 with N=10 and GSM8K/HumanEval Pass@1/5 metrics. Existing splits, training budgets, simulator perturbations, and 100-generation main math/code evaluations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends generality and optimization analyses through model-size/architecture tests, time-to-baseline-peak training-reward comparisons, and full gradient-norm/GSS traces (Sections 5.4–5.5 and Appendix G.4–G.5). The original answer-count ablation, covariance diagnostics, inconsistency analysis, reward-richness analysis, and case studies are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify data seed 42 and retain the covariance diagnostic using 50 samples with 10 independent replications each. Neither adds uncertainty across repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new gradient plots show within-run dynamics rather than new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and ablation values are retained, but substantial results are added. Examples include trajectory DFD 157.03 for TreeRPO-64 versus 151.10 for GRPO-MA (Table 6), 167.32 versus 134.67 for the new 7B GRPO/MA configurations (Table 7), Qwen3 results (Table 8), and GSM8K/HumanEval scores (Table 11). Figures 13–18 add timing and gradient findings.

T1.justification: The limited mathematical revision concerns the combined objective's KL accounting (v1 Eqs. 1 and 3; v3 Eq. 2). The independence and nondegeneracy assumptions, delta-method variance expressions, K/M asymptotic arguments, and full appendix derivations are otherwise retained. The stronger necessity framing is not accompanied by a new proof.

C1.justification: v1 presents GRPO-MA as an algorithm addressing gradient coupling, sparse rewards, and unstable advantages. v3 recasts the main contribution as a claimed first variance-based explanation of tree branching and its potential necessity under GRPO-style estimators without value models. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion also broaden effectiveness claims across model sizes and architectures.

C2.justification: v3 adds arguments about controllable variance sources and branching necessity, plus conjectures explaining TreeRPO's sensitivity to segmentation. It qualifies the ablation trend from all metrics decreasing to most tending to decrease. The explicit limitations paragraph disappears, including the verifiable-reward restriction, although the independence caveat remains.

D1.justification: New details include TreeRPO's 64/128-token segment limits and wall-clock plots sampled every 50 steps with ±25-step averaging. The existing task prompts, decoding stop strings, Transformers version, LoRA settings, hardware, and hyperparameter table are retained. No new code or data release information is supplied.

R1.justification: A new tree-search subsection discusses VinePPO, SPO, TreeRL, TreePO, and TreeRPO, positioning GRPO-MA as a minimal setting for explaining branching. Discussions and references concerning CPPO, off-policy GRPO, and Spectral Policy Optimization are removed. This substantially changes research positioning rather than merely updating citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, conclusion, and substantial experimental discussion are rewritten around the tree-branching argument. Related work gains subsections, new evaluation sections are inserted, and the main-text case study and inconsistency analysis move to reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Task descriptions become a metric table, the answer-count ablation changes from a horizontal strip to a grid, and existing figures are resized or relocated. New comparison tables and wall-clock/gradient figures substantially expand the displays; retained numerical tables mainly undergo reformatting.

improvement.justification: The added GRPO/tree baselines, trained 7B and text-only models, and appendix diagnostics strengthen v1's limited comparative and model-generalization evidence. Better positioning against tree-search research also helps. These gains are tempered by stronger necessity claims resting on essentially unchanged approximate theory and removal of explicit limitations, making the net quality improvement limited.
